text:
maria_support: Customer reports streaming JSON responses frequently cut off mid-object when piping through a corporate proxy. They surface a parse error (unexpected end of input) in their Node consumer. request_id: req_0a1b2c3d, model: redwood/text-stream-1, sdk: node-fetch v3. They say it happens ~1/20 streams and seems correlated with larger payloads.

jake_engineer: thanks — can you paste the minimal curl/req sample from the customer and any proxy details? also pasting the raw chunked response sample would help.

maria_support: here's the customer repro (sanitized):
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY"
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream"
  -d '{"model":"redwood/text-stream-1","input":"generate large json array...","mode":"structured"}'
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate/stream
```
They say the client is behind `corp-proxy.example` (transparent TLS intercept) and using a Node service that buffers streaming data then JSON.parse() at chunk boundary. They attached a short hex dump showing last bytes: `...0x7d 0x5d 0x0a` then connection reset.

jake_engineer: that pattern (complete object close bytes then reset) suggests an upstream/edge TLS teardown while browser/proxy still streaming. quick checklist: 1) are they using a streaming JSON top-level array? streaming an array can break if connection closes without final `]`. 2) are they relying on chunk boundaries to equal object boundaries? chunk boundaries are not reliable. 3) can they share the HAR or raw socket capture?

maria_support: asked customer for HAR and a tcpdump. they sent a small HAR that shows `Connection: keep-alive` on client -> proxy, but the proxy injects `Connection: close` on the downstream call and then issues a FIN immediately after last chunk.

nate_sre: tagging in what we've seen before: some corporate proxies will terminate long-ish idle connections by swapping keep-alive behavior which can cause the final TCP FIN before client finishes reading. On our side the runtime emits streaming tokens as they are generated (no Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding: chunked / SSE framing). If a proxy forces a connection close mid-stream the client could get truncated JSON.

sofia_product: short-term mitigation for customers: suggest using either a) non-streaming endpoints for structured JSON outputs (get the full payload server-side) or b) stream JSON objects as newline-delimited JSON (JSONL) where each event is a complete object, or c) use an incremental parser that tolerates partial chunks (e.g., `stream-json`, `clarinet`). we should document recommended patterns in docs.

jake_engineer: agree. also adding a small repro and recommended Node fetch config to reduce risk (keep-alive and aggresive tcp keepalive):
```js
// Node-fetch + agent keepAlive example
import fetch from 'node-fetch';
import http from 'http';
const agent = new http.Agent({ keepAlive: true, keepAliveMsecs: 60000 });
const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate/stream', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer $KEY', 'Accept':'text/event-stream' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood/text-stream-1', input: '...' }),
  agent
});
res.body.on('data', chunk => { /* append to buffer, use streaming parser */ });
```
But this is only mitigation; if proxy actively kills the downstream TCP connection we'll still lose final bytes.

ops-bot: [runtime-log] req_0a1b2c3d served by runtime-2.14.7 on node-gpu-12 at 2026-06-04T14:32:10Z — bytes_sent: 128k — stream_closed: client_disconnect (code=RST)

maria_support: forwarded the runtime log to the customer. they confirmed the timestamp aligns and the proxy shows the same time window.

jake_engineer: next steps: 1) escalate to eng-runtime to see whether we can emit an explicit SSE stream terminator event (an extra `event: done\n\ndata: {"eof":true}\n\n`) so SSE consumers get a final logical event even if underlying connection is torn down; 2) add a docs note about streaming structured JSON anti-patterns (top-level array). 3) add a troubleshoot KB entry recommending HAR capture and using JSONL for streaming. can someone from eng-runtime take req_0a1b2c3d and check wire-level capture and the edge proxy behavior?

jake_engineer: filing eng runtime issue: RG-3142. @nate_sre can you attach relevant edge logs and the TLS proxy fingerprint?

nate_sre: attached internal edge log snippet and proxy fingerprint hash to RG-3142. also scheduled a small canary tomorrow to emit both a final SSE `eof` event and a duplicate last chunk so clients behind aggressive proxies have a chance to see a full object.

sofia_product: thanks — i'll draft a short KB and add examples: 1) JSONL stream example 2) Node fetch keepAlive sample 3) curl repro and HAR checklist. i'll post PR to docs once RG-3142 has an initial mitigation. :memo:

maria_support: customer accepted mitigations: switched to non-streaming structured endpoint temporarily and will test JSONL in their staging behind corp-proxy. they're ok with monitoring for a week. will follow up with HAR if they see more failures. closing loop here once next-week canary completes. :white_check_mark:
